text: SUPERVISOR — user diagnosis steer on the layer FAIL, verbatim: "the layer multiplication problem is a state update problem... as always." Redirect your hunt: this is not (primarily) hit targets or a missed strip copy — inspect the REORDER STATE UPDATE itself. The class the user means, seen repeatedly in this stack: non-functional setState against a stale snapshot, double-applied updates (strict/double-invoke or an event firing twice), or move implemented as remove+insert where the insert re-runs against already-updated state and APPENDS a copy, or an effect echoing the reorder back into the array. Print the state update sequence on one up-click: every setter call with its input array and output array, in order. The duplication will be visible in one capture. Fix with an idempotent functional update (move = one pure reorder of prev). Then still verify on the user's actual sculpt-paint surface, and keep the one-strip unification if the inventory found copies — but the state bug is the root.
